title: Shift squares for primitive strict-system structural comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. On small pro-etale sites of finite-type $k$-schemes let $\mathscr S_W$ be strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with system inverse image $P_v$, total derived direct image $S_v$, exact open extension $J_j$, and derived system tensor, realized on the simultaneous ringed diagram sites of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Maps $v$ are separated finite type and opens $j$ are quasi-compact. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of these module systems. Give these functors the cochain-shift comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift]; tensor uses the signed total comparison $t_{a,b}:M[a]\otimes^LN[b]\cong(M\otimes^LN)[a+b]$ with coefficient $(-1)^{bp}$ on $M[a]^p\otimes N[b]^q$ [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus].

Each of the following primitive natural transformations commutes with every integer shift in each designated input occurrence: the canonical system pullback compositors and square identifications induced by equality of scheme composites; the pullback/tensor comparisons; the tensor associator, unitors and Koszul symmetry; open-extension composition; and, for open immersions $b:V_W\to V$ and $s:U\to V_W$ with $k=bs$, the canonical restriction identification $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$. If $s$ is also closed, the canonical clopen comparison $J_s\cong S_s$ and the component projection $\pi_s:1\to J_sP_s$ (identity on $s(U)$, zero on its open complement) also commute with all these shifts, in the normalization of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. Precisely, if $\tau:F\to G$ is any listed map and one input $M$ is replaced by $M[r]$, its canonical comparisons satisfy $\chi_G\circ\tau_{M[r]}=\tau_M[r]\circ\chi_F$; for symmetry the shifted occurrence is followed to its permuted position. These are identities of semilinear-system transformations before evaluation or scalar restriction. No integral realization, arbitrary expression-tree comparison, proper/open mate, or projection/exchange transformation is asserted.

proof.text: Work on the simultaneous ringed-diagram sites supplied by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. There the system operations are termwise inverse image, K-injective direct image, exact open extension and K-flat tensor, and their canonical pullback composition maps and tensor/pullback maps are induced by degree-zero maps of the corresponding resolutions. The shift comparison for each operation, including the signed tensor comparison, is the one in [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift]. Reindexing a resolution and multiplying its differential by the usual shift sign commutes with every degree-zero component map and with the quotient transition maps. Hence the shift square holds for every canonical pullback compositor and for every square identification obtained by equality of scheme composites, in each input slot; the same argument gives naturality in the input morphisms and the cocycle for adding two shifts.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: coefficient comparisons and the basic operations used in the expression-tree recursion; chain-level shift calculation

proof.text: For the pullback/tensor comparison, choose K-flat system resolutions. The comparison sends a pure tensor in degrees (p,q) to the tensor of the two pulled-back pure tensors, so it preserves (p,q). The shifted tensor comparison multiplies this component by (-1)^(b p), exactly on both routes; the signed formula and its naturality are the statement of [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus]. Therefore the pullback/tensor square commutes for arbitrary integers and either shifted input. The realization node identifies this ringed-diagram comparison with the canonical system comparison before evaluation.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: tensor reassociation and coefficient comparisons; signed total-tensor comparison

proof.text: The tensor associator and unitors are the degree-zero rebracketing and insertion/removal of the unit on total K-flat complexes, so they commute with reindexing and with the shift differential signs. For the symmetry, on a shifted bidegree (p,q) the two composites have exponents b p + (p+a)(q+b) and a b + p q + a q; their difference is 2 b p. Thus the Koszul symmetry square is the required equality, including the graded factor (-1)^(a b). These are precisely the associativity and symmetry identities for the signed comparison t in [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus], and descent there transfers the calculation to the derived system category.

proof.text: For composable open immersions, termwise extension by zero is exact and its composition map is the identity on sections over the composite open and zero elsewhere. The shift functor only reindexes the same termwise sections and changes the differential sign, so this composition map is unchanged and its shift square is immediate. The normalized open extension and tensor maps on the system ringed topoi are the maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], while [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift] supplies their operation shifts; therefore the assertion holds before evaluation and is coherent under iterated composition.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: open maps and basic operations; termwise extension-by-zero calculation

proof.text: Let b:V_W to V and s:U to V_W be the open immersions with k=b s. On the ringed diagram sites the canonical identification P_b J_k to J_s is the open-base-change map normalized by the open unit: after restriction to the open it is the identity on sections. Its components are degree-zero maps of termwise complexes, and its inverse is the open-adjunction adjunct described in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Reindexing therefore gives the same map after any shift in either input. The system realization in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] identifies this normalized map with the intrinsic system transformation, so the square is an equality of system maps before evaluation.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: open/clopen identifications before adjunction transposition

proof.text: If s is also closed, the clopen decomposition makes J_s the component functor and S_s the same componentwise direct image. The comparison J_s to S_s is therefore the identity on the s(U) component and zero on the complementary component, and the projection pi_s is exactly the map (x,y) maps to (x,0). Shifts preserve each component, the identity map and the zero map, so both the clopen comparison and pi_s commute with every shift. The proper/open mate-pasting node states these maps and their normalization as semilinear-system transformations before evaluation, and the realization node identifies them with the canonical system maps. This also proves naturality and compatibility with adding shifts.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: clopen projection and proper/open normalization

proof.text: All preceding calculations are componentwise on the same simultaneous models, hence they remain equalities of semilinear-system transformations rather than equalities inferred from finite evaluations or scalar restriction. Whiskering by any of the listed operations and composing the displayed squares preserves the shift equations. No step introduces an integral realization comparison, an arbitrary expression-tree comparison, a proper/open mate, or an exchange/projection transformation beyond the explicitly listed primitive maps.
